messages:
maria-rl: Quick heads up — starting onboarding for Paperclip-6B (weights from paperclip.ai). The license file attached in the repo says 'NonCommercial-2.1' with an odd clause on hosting/serving. Can we surface this on the hosted API? 

sara-legal: Can you paste the exact clause? NonCommercial usually blocks commercial offering but we need to see whether 'hosting as a service' is explicitly mentioned. 

maria-rl: Here's the snippet: "The Model may not be used for commercial inference, hosting, or redistribution without separate permission." 

kevin-m: That reads pretty clear. Hosting as a service = not allowed. :grimacing:

josh-ml: Wait — what about offering access via our hosted API as a managed endpoint for customers who are internal/experimental vs paying? Any carve-outs? 

sara-legal: No carve-out in that clause. Two options: 1) Ask upstream for a commercial license. 2) Use model in Dedicated/Private only (customer-managed infra) if the license allows non-redistribution but permits internal use. Need to confirm exact definitions in license preamble. 

anika-eng: From product POV, we could still onboard for evals/benchmarks and internal RAG tests if we avoid public hosting and redistribution. Also need to check quantized weights: if we ship 4-bit quantized variants, is that considered redistribution? 

sara-legal: Usually quantized binaries are derivatives. If redistribution is blocked, shipping quantized weights is not allowed. Hosting (serving requests) may still be prohibited depending on clause wording. 

kevin-m: For our Dedicated offering, customers bring infra and we only provide control plane — does that count as hosting? 

sara-legal: If we don't persist or transfer weights and solely provide orchestration, it's less risky, but still grey. Need to map definitions: "host" vs "provide access." I'll loop in legal counsel. 

maria-rl: From an ML ops side, we already tried `quantize --bits 4` locally and perf is fine. Want to run batch evals and quality regression tests. Can we run evals on CI using a pinned copy in our internal eval cluster? 

sara-legal: Running internal evals for research/benchmarking usually ok under NonCommercial as long as model isn't redistributed. Keep logs and any artifacts internal and don't publish weights or example outputs that reveal proprietary prompts. 

josh-ml: Noted. Also one more: attribution. The license says "must display model and author attribution prominently when used." Do we need a UI banner even for internal tests? 

sara-legal: Attribution obligations apply on use. For internal tests, keep internal docs labeling. For any customer-facing surface (even ephemeral test endpoints), we should display attribution in the UI or in API responses per license. 

anika-eng: Technical ask — if we wrap the model in a wrapper that adds an attribution header to responses, is that compliant? 

sara-legal: Yes, programmatic attribution (header or footer) is acceptable so long as it is prominent and not hidden. Track this in the onboarding checklist. 

maria-rl: I'll proceed with internal evals only, add attribution header in test endpoints, and open a contact request to upstream for commercial terms. 

kevin-m: For the quantization question, flagging ops: we might need to archive the quantized artifacts behind an internal-only bucket and not push them to any external repos. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: Reminder: Added onboarding ticket #ML-4398 and attached license copy. 

sara-legal: I'll draft a short note for the legal record and ping upstream licensing. Expect follow-up by EOD tomorrow. 

josh-ml: Thanks — sounds like a good plan. Keep us posted if upstream replies with permissive terms. 

maria-rl: Will do — thanks all.
